papers.title_in_file: Quantum Parameter Study for Quantum Inspired Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A three-page author-published note (K. Kawchak, ChemicalQDevice, 2023-09-26) on how the number of trainable Ry parameters in a 4-qubit circuit assisting a ResNet50 changes validation accuracy on three image datasets.

assertions.value: The authors label the ResNet50 neural network as holding 23M non-trainable parameters.
quotes: Figure 1a: ResNet50 Neural Network 23M Non-Trainable Parameters 1
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the Figure 1a caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that a ResNet50 neural network without trainable parameters is assisted in classifying images by a 4-qubit quantum circuit with trainable parameters, and that Accuracy, Loss and Runtime metrics are analyzed for three different sized datasets.
quotes: Synopsis: A ResNet50 Neural Network without trainable parameters is assisted classifying images with a 4-qubit Quantum Circuit with trainable parameters for the analysis of Accuracy, Loss, and Runtime metrics for three different sized datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Synopsis states the paper's own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The text pages of the paper report no Runtime result; the Runtime metric named in the synopsis is not reported in the text layer (it may sit in Figure 1d or the other figures).

assertions.value: The authors describe the quantum circuit in Figure 1b as an embedding layer on the left, up to 40 trainable parameters in the middle, and measurements on the right.
quotes: Figure 1b: Quantum Circuit. Left: Embedding Layer 2 Middle: Up to 40 Trainable Parameters, Right: Measurements
assertions.certainty_reason: The Figure 1b caption states the circuit design.

assertions.value: The authors list three datasets: 2-Class Hymenoptera, 10-Class Tumor MRI and 44-Class Tumor MRI.
quotes: Figure 1c: Datasets. 1) 2-Class Hymenoptera 2) 10-Class Tumor MRI, 3) 44-Class Tumor MRI
assertions.certainty_reason: The Figure 1c caption states the datasets used.

assertions.value: The authors name Default.qubit (a simulator device, cited to the PennyLane documentation) and an NVIDIA V100 16 GB as the device and hardware of the study.
quotes: Default.qubit 13, NVIDIA V100 16 GB 14
assertions.certainty_reason: The footer line states the paper's own device setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Default.qubit is PennyLane's classical state-vector simulator, so the circuit was simulated on a GPU machine and not run on quantum hardware. The paper does not say this in words.

assertions.value: The authors state that different numbers of trainable Ry layers were implemented in a Quantum transfer learning model, to study the effect of increasing circuit parameters on a single dataset and any observable trends between datasets.
quotes: In this study, different numbers of trainable Ry layers were implemented in a
model in order to study the effect increasing circuit parameters has on a single dataset, as well as any observable trends between datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Introduction states the purpose and scope of the study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the 2-Class Hymenoptera dataset, used as a standard, did not experience improvements in accuracy with more trainable quantum parameters.
quotes: 1) 2-Class Hymenoptera as a Standard did not experience improvements in accuracy with more trainable quantum parameters
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives no accuracy values, number of runs or variance, so the size of the effect cannot be judged from the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that the 10-Class Tumor MRI dataset experienced the largest increase in accuracies as the number of parameters was increased.
quotes: 2) 10-Class Tumor MRI dataset experienced the largest increase in accuracies as the number of parameters were increased
assertions.reader_inference: No accuracy values are in the text; the claim rests on Figure 1d, which the text layer does not carry.

assertions.value: The authors report that the 44-Class Tumor MRI dataset had small improvements in accuracy for a lower number of trainable parameters.
quotes: 3) 44-Class Tumor MRI dataset had small improvements in accuracy for lower number of trainable parameters

assertions.value: The authors report that the 10-Class and 44-Class datasets both generally increased in accuracy for the first 20 trainable parameters, while the Hymenoptera dataset did not appear to exhibit a positive response to additional trainable parameters.
quotes: Although the Hymenoptera dataset did not appear to exhibit a positive response to additional trainable parameters, the 10-Class and 44-Class datasets both generally increased in accuracy for the first 20 trainable parameters.

assertions.value: The authors state that, with fewer total tumor classes and more images per class, the 10-Class dataset yielded the best accuracy increases for the highest number of parameters.
quotes: With less total number of tumor classes and a greater number of images per class, the 10-Class dataset yielded the best accuracy increases for the highest number of parameters.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives no experiment that separates class count from images per class, so this explanation is untested in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that differences between training and validation losses were the lowest for the 10-class set at 40 parameters, and state this may indicate less concern of overfitting.
quotes: Differences between training and validation losses were the lowest for the 10-class set for 40 parameters, which may indicate less concerns of overfitting.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors hedge with 'may'. No loss values are in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum inspired methods and devices will likely be able to optimize large numbers of parameters, and that a productive approach will likely be to find the minimum number of parameters needed to assist classical deep learning.
quotes: As quantum inspired methods and devices will likely be able to optimize large numbers of parameters, a productive approach will likely be to find the minimum number of parameters needed to assist classical deep learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study provided insight into parameter selection when best quality datasets are used.
quotes: This study provided insight into parameter selection when best quality datasets are used.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Discussion states the scope of the study's findings.
assertions.reader_inference: Read as a scope limit: the findings are stated for best quality datasets only. The text does not define best quality.

assertions.value: The authors state that this study builds from prior algorithm prototypings, benchmarking, and cost/efficiency studies, and that the larger tumor datasets were also independently analyzed with larger circuits in separate studies.
quotes: This study builds from prior algorithm prototypings, benchmarking, and cost/efficiency studies.
The larger tumor datasets were also independently analyzed w/ larger circuits in separate studies.
assertions.reader_inference: The cited items are the author's own LinkedIn posts and company R&D updates (references 7 to 12), not peer-reviewed work.

papers.title_in_file: Tree tensor network state approach for solving hierarchical equations of motion
papers.version_note: arXiv:2304.05151v2 (3 Jun 2023). The text holds the main paper and the reference list only; the supplementary material (Frenkel exciton model, spin-boson-like chain, Pade expressions) is not in the text.
papers.what_it_is: A method paper that represents the extended wave function of the hierarchical equations of motion as a tree tensor network state, propagates it with a time-dependent variational principle algorithm, and benchmarks it on a spin-boson model against conventional HEOM and a matrix product state chain.

assertions.value: The authors describe the HEOM method as based on an exponential series expansion of the bath correlation function, used to construct a group of auxiliary density operators (ADOs) that obey a hierarchical set of differential equations.
quotes: The core idea of the method is based on an exponential series expansion of the bath correlation function
so as to construct a group of auxiliary density operators (ADOs) that obey a hierarchical set of differential equations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of an existing method that the paper attributes to earlier work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper concerns classical tensor network simulation of open quantum system dynamics; it bears on the qc context only as a simulation method.

assertions.value: The authors state that HEOM applications are limited when the central system is large, many exponential terms (effective bath modes) are required, and a deep hierarchical depth is needed, because the computational cost grows exponentially with these factors.
quotes: its applications hit a hard wall in the cases where the central system size is large, many exponential terms (or effective bath modes) are required to reproduce the original bath correlation function
This is because the computational cost grows exponentially with the increase of these factors.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement in the introduction without a derivation or measurement in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, when entanglement stays confined within near neighboring tensors over a long time, the computational cost of the HEOM+MPS/TT method scales linearly with the system size, the number of effective bath modes, and the hierarchical depth.
quotes: confined within the near neighboring tensors over a long time, the computational cost of the HEOM+MPS/TT method scales linearly with the system size, the number of effective bath modes, and the hierarchical depth.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about earlier HEOM+MPS/TT work, not shown in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the HEOM+MPS/TT method often does not meet that condition, because the system degrees of freedom may be strongly coupled to every effective bath mode, so correlation spreads quickly along the MPS chain and very large bond dimensions are needed for accurate results.
quotes: the system DoF may also be strongly coupled to every effective bath mode. As a consequence, the correlation would quickly spread over a long distance along the MPS chain, and very large bond dimensions are needed to obtain accurate results.
assertions.certainty_reason: The motivating limitation is asserted, not measured in this paper; the later MPS test used the same bond dimension as the tree.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors' own MPS/TT test later in the paper converged at the same maximal bond dimension as the tree, so the motivating claim of very large bond dimensions is not exhibited by the one model they ran.

assertions.value: The authors take the spin-boson model as the demonstration system, with the spin coupled to a bath of harmonic oscillators through a linear form in the bath coordinates.
quotes: a simple but paradigmatic open quantum system, the spinboson model
takes a linear form with respect to the bath coordinate qj
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own model in Section 1 (Eqs. 1 to 5).

papers.title_in_file: Geometric spectral theory of quantum graphs
papers.version_note: Text layer is the published Communications in Mathematics 32 (2024) copy of arXiv:2310.02707v3; single copy, not duplicated.
papers.what_it_is: Lecture notes on the dependence of Laplacian eigenvalues on the geometry of a compact metric graph (Nicaise, Friedlander and surgery-based eigenvalue bounds).
papers.why_not: The paper is pure mathematics: spectral theory of differential operators (Laplacians) on metric graphs, called quantum graphs. It contains no quantum computing, quantum machine learning, machine learning, finance or evaluation-method content; its eigenvalue theorems (Nicaise, Friedlander, surgery principles) concern diffusion on graphs of fixed total length. The store holds no assertions from it, so there are no verdicts to give, and no assertion is entered.

papers.title_in_file: Precise Photon Arrival Time Measurement via Time to Frequency Demultiplexing
papers.version_note: arXiv:2606.15030v1, 13 Jun 2026; text layer matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper that maps photon arrival time to wavelength channels with multiplexed sum-frequency conversion in a multi-period PPLN waveguide and estimates arrival time from channel count ratios, with RMSE of about 0.6 to 1 ps in a three-channel test.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate a nonlinear-optics approach that translates the temporal information of single photons to a wavelength distribution by frequency conversion, followed by de-multiplexed detection, using a multi-color, pulse-delayed pump laser to drive multiplexed frequency conversion.
quotes: We demonstrate a nonlinear-optics approach to precise measurement of photon arrival time, by translating the temporal information of single photons to a wavelength distribution of frequency conversion followed by de-multiplexed detection.
It uses a multi-color, pulse-delayed pump laser to drive multiplexed frequency conversion, transducing photons to various frequency channels according to their arrival time.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own method and scope.

assertions.value: The authors claim in the abstract that, by photon detection in each channel, the measurement resolution and accuracy can reach picosecond level, much lower than the detectors' naive resolution and significantly beating the shot-noise limited direct detection.
quotes: By photon detection in each channel, the measurement resolution and accuracy can reach picosecond level, much lower than the detectors’ naive resolution and significantly beating the shot-noise limited direct detection.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison to direct detection in the body (Fig. 7) is against a computed formula, not a measured direct-detection run, and the experiment used three channels with a roughly 12.5 ps pump (Section 4), so 'picosecond level' is the measured RMSE of about 1 ps, not a pulse-width-limited figure.

assertions.value: The authors state in the abstract that the approach supports event-ready operations, capable of detecting randomly arriving single photons with no dead window. The conclusion states more weakly that it largely mitigates the dead time associated with repetitive temporal scanning.
quotes: our approach supports event-ready operations, capable of detecting randomly arriving single photons with no dead window.
Also, it largely mitigates the dead time associated with repetitive temporal scanning and is suitable for photons that arrive randomly or only once.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says no dead window; the conclusion says largely mitigates. The reported experiments held the delay fixed per integration window and scanned it between windows, so the event-ready, single-photon property is argued, not run as a random-arrival test.

assertions.value: The authors state two requirements for the system: low background noise, with injected noise comparable to or lower than the detector dark counts, and single-shot operation, able to determine a random photon arrival time without repetitive or adaptive measurements.
quotes: Low background noise, where the injected noise is comparable to or lower than the detector dark counts;
Single-shot operation, where the system is capable of precisely determining a random photon arrival time without relying on repetitive or adaptive measurements.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states the design goals as the paper's own scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no measured background or dark-count figure against the first requirement.

assertions.value: The authors describe a multiplexed quantum frequency converter (m-QFC) pumped by multiple pulse trains, each of a different color, to convert the signal into different wavelengths by sum- or difference-frequency generation; all pulse trains share the same period but are relatively delayed.
quotes: The m-QFC is pumped by multiple pulse trains, each of a different color, to convert the signal into different wavelengths through the generation of sum- or difference-frequency.
All pulse trains share the same period, but are relatively delayed with respect to one another.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states the architecture of the paper's own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the detectors provide the coarse photon arrival time, limited by their timing jitter, while the identity of the detector that clicks provides the fine timing information, determined by the pump pulse width.
quotes: the detectors provide the coarse photon arrival time, limited by their timing jitter, while the identity of the detector that clicks provides the fine timing information, determined by the pump pulse width.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiment in Section 4 does not use the coarse detector time tags (Section 4, p.10); only the fine, wavelength-channel part is tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pulse trains can be generated with frequency-comb lines, each train formed by a subset of comb lines; the period is set by the comb-line spacing and the pulse width by the spectral width of the subset.
quotes: Such pulse trains can be generated with frequency-comb lines, where each train is formed by a subset of comb lines.
The period is determined by the comb-line spacing, whereas the pulse width is determined by the spectral width of the subset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states how the paper's pulse trains are made.

assertions.value: The authors give a practical design example: a PPLN waveguide with 10 quasi-phase-matching peaks, ten pulse trains carved from comb lines with 25-GHz spacing, pulses of about 4 ps, and Si-APD detectors with typical timing jitter of about 40 ps FWHM, so that the which-detector information gives a fine resolution of 4 ps.
quotes: In a practical example, the m-QFC can consist of a PPLN waveguide with 10 quasi-phase-matching peaks [26].
Ten pulse trains are carved out of a laser beam of comb lines with 25-GHz spacing; see Fig. 1(a). Each pulse is about 4 ps long
The timing jitter of commercially available Si-APD detectors is typically about 40 ps FWHM.
The which-detector information, on the other hand, gives a fine resolution of 4 ps.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a proposed design, not the tested one. The experiment used three channels and a pump pulse of about 12.5 ps (Section 4). A 25 GHz spacing implies a 40 ps period (inference; the paper does not state it).

assertions.value: The authors use a ratio-manifold estimator: the measured channel counts are normalized to a ratio vector and compared with a calibrated delay-dependent reference; the arrival-time estimate is the delay in the calibration set that minimizes a distance function between the calibrated and measured ratio vectors.
quotes: Here, we use a ratio-manifold estimator that compares the measured spectral count distribution with a calibrated delay-dependent reference.
The arrival time is estimated by comparing rmeas with the calibrated manifold over the delay set T .
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 defines the estimator the results depend on.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints Eq. 4 garbled; it reads as the squared Euclidean (L2) norm of R(tau) minus r_meas, and Eq. 5 as the argmin over the delay set.

assertions.value: The authors state that the normalization suppresses common-mode power fluctuations and channel-independent throughput variations while preserving the relative inter-channel pattern that encodes the timing information.
quotes: This normalization suppresses common-mode power fluctuations and channel-independent throughput variations, while preserving the relative inter-channel pattern that encodes the timing information.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing a textbook reference (62), that in the high-count regime the ratio mapping approaches a deterministic manifold, whereas at low photon number the estimation uncertainty is governed by shot-noise fluctuations in the underlying counts.
